en: The Apadāna of the Elder Padumapupphiya Timiravagga 10 [Verse 1] I was a merchant’s son in the city of Bandhumatī, And I gave a lotus flower to the Buddha Vipassī. [Verse 2] Because of that root of merit, for ninety-one aeons, I never fell into the states of misery; I was always reborn in heaven. [Verse 3] In this fortunate aeon, having passed through many births, I was born into a wealthy family in the city of Sāvatthī. [Verse 4] When the Teacher, the Great Sage, arrived at Sāvatthī, I went to him with great joy and paid homage to the Buddha. [Verse 5] I took a lotus flower and offered it to the Conqueror; Having made that offering, I then departed from his presence. [Verse 6] Through that deed, I was reborn in the realm of the Thirty-Three, And there I enjoyed divine pleasures for a full ten thousand years. [Verse 7] From that world, I passed away and was reborn in the human world, Where I possessed great wealth and lived in the city of Sāvatthī. [Verse 8] When the Teacher, the Great Sage, arrived at Sāvatthī, I went to him with great joy and paid homage to the Buddha. [Verse 9] I took a lotus flower and offered it to the Conqueror; Having made that offering, I then departed from his presence. [Verse 10] By the power of that deed, I have attained the fruit of Arhatship; My mind is liberated, and I am free from all defilements.

[Verse 11] I have seen the Buddha, the peerless one among men, And I have heard the Dhamma, which leads to the cessation of suffering. [Verse 12] I have fulfilled my task and lived the holy life; There is no further existence for me beyond this present life. [Verse 13] I remember my past lives, as clear as if they were today; With the divine eye, I see beings passing away and being reborn. [Verse 14] I know the minds of others exactly as they are; I have destroyed the taints and attained the state of peace. [Verse 15] This is my final birth; there will be no more becoming; I have crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra and reached the further shore. [Verse 16] I have attained the cool state, the deathless, the supreme security; I have realized Nibbāna, the end of all suffering. [Verse 17] I pay homage to the Buddha, the peerless one among men; I pay homage to the Dhamma, well-taught by the One with Vision. [Verse 18] I pay homage to the Saṅgha, the field of merit unsurpassed; May I attain the same state as the Teacher, the Great Sage. [Verse 19] I have attained the goal of my ascetic life; I have done what was to be done and laid down the heavy burden. [Verse 20] I have severed the bonds of Māra; I have attained the state of peace, the end of all suffering. “Having entered the lotus grove,
I was breaking off the lotuses here;
there I saw the Buddha Phussa.”
Possessing the thirty-two excellent marks,
I took a lotus flower and tossed it into the air.
Having remembered my evil deeds,
I went forth into the homeless life;
having gone forth, with my body...
With my mind restrained,
having abandoned verbal misconduct,
I purified my livelihood.
In the ninety-two aeons since then,
because I offered that flower,
I have not known a state of misery.
This is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha.
And there were eighteen lords of the earth named Padumābhāsa.
In eighteen aeons,
there were forty-eight months [of my life];
the four analytical knowledges—
the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Padumapupphiya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Padumapupphiya is the tenth.
The ninth chapter, the Timira-vagga.
Its summary (uddāna) is as follows:
The *timira-naṅgalī-puppha* is one who has joined the palms downward;
perceiving two rays of light, he is a giver of fruit.
The Saddasaññī and the Secaka,
the Padmapupphi, and the verses—
fifty-six in all— are recited.
